mainEntity.name: Do I need to send creative?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can send it, or we can brief and source it through our creative team as a separate scope.

mainEntity.name: Which accounts do you work in?

acceptedAnswer.text: The client's Meta Business account, with access shared through you. They keep ownership.

mainEntity.name: Do you run Instagram-only or WhatsApp campaigns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within Meta's ad formats and policies. We scope the placements per client.

mainEntity.name: Can you share learnings across my clients?

acceptedAnswer.text: We keep each client separate and confidential. We do not share one client's data with another.

mainEntity.name: Will my client know MMC is involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you choose to tell them. We sign an NDA, work under your brand, send deliverables in your format and do not contact your clients unless you ask us to.

mainEntity.name: How do we get started with white-label Meta Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add us to the client's ad account through your agency. After the NDA we audit tracking and structure before launching.

stages.why: Ads cannot start, or launch with the wrong look, and the first week of spend is wasted.
stages.does: Creative briefs and brand rules are collected at handover, and we flag gaps before the launch date, not after.

stages.breaks: Audiences are built on the client's guess.
stages.why: Clicks from people who will never buy make the report look busy and the account look weak.
stages.does: Audiences come from the client's customer lists and site events, and we explain the structure in plain words.

stages.breaks: Tracking is wrong, so the report is too.
stages.why: If events double count or go missing, you end up defending numbers you cannot trust.
stages.does: Pixel and Conversions API events are checked before scaling, and any fix the client must make is written for you to send.

stages.breaks: One winning ad runs until it dies.
stages.why: Frequency climbs, cost rises and the client asks what changed.
stages.does: A rotation plan feeds in new hooks and formats on a schedule you can see, with retired ads noted.

stages.breaks: The weekly note says what happened, not why.
stages.why: You need a reason to give the client, not a screenshot.
stages.does: Each week's note covers what changed, what we learned and what happens next, ready for your own words.
